messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: repeated OOMs on serving-prod-gpu-12 (node-gpu-07). pattern: cudaDriverReset -> container crash. 3/5 nodes in pool reported OOM in last 10m. auto-evict triggered.

jin: i'm seeing gradual RSS growth in the kv-cache page allocator — slow creep across the pool for ~8h, not a single noisy spike. looks like fragmentation + long-lived KVs.

sara: logs show repeated 'cuda: out of memory' and containers exiting with code 137. dmesg indicates GPU reset on node-gpu-07. tail of runtime log below.

sara: ```
[2025-06-15T11:08:12Z] serving-runtime[pid=2345]: runtime: alloc failed: out of memory
[2025-06-15T11:08:13Z] runtime: fatal: container exited with code 137
[2025-06-15T11:08:13Z] kernel: NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x14)
[2025-06-15T11:08:13Z] kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:03:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

jin: hypothesis: allocator fragmentation from paged-attention + sticky KV slabs. eviction isn't trimming stale KVs fast enough when seq-len distribution is wide. compounds over time -> gradual OOM.

sara: quick mitigation that helped on canary: pushed kv_cache_trim=1 and trimmed inactive slabs, saw ~15% mem reduction on canary. will attempt cluster rollout if stable.

alex: i'm cordoning node-gpu-07 and restarting the runtime on node-gpu-09. also scaling up the dedicated pool by +2 GPUs to relieve pressure.

mira: customer-ops: we have ~6 customers reporting 503/504 in the last 20m. I'm drafting a short message and will notify top-tier customers.

jin: proposed live mitigations (short-term):
1) enable aggressive kv_trim (kv_trim_rate=0.5) cluster-wide
2) set temporary eviction watermark lower (80% mem)
3) enable fallback routing to smaller model variants for lower tier traffic
4) restart affected containers with --clear-kv-cache flag

sara: applying step 1 to canary now. command:

sara: ```
kubectl -n prod exec svc/serving-runtime-canary -- /bin/sh -c "curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/kv_trim?rate=0.5"
# then monitor memory trend for 2-3 minutes
```

alex: rolling restart to pick up kv-trim flag across canary + next batch:
```
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/serving-runtime --grace-period=15
```

sara: canary after trim: mem before 62GB -> after 53GB. good delta. watching for re-accumulation.

incident-bot: auto-escalation rule: if OOMs persist after 5m from mitigation, page infra-lead.

mira: incident page updated, posting workaround for customers: temporary degraded throughput while we stabilize.

alex: i'm executing cluster-wide kv_trim now on a rolling window. also kicked off 2x GPU scale up. will restart 2 noisy containers with --clear-kv-cache.

alex: commands run: 
```
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}' | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl -n prod exec {} -- /bin/sh -c "curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/kv_trim?rate=0.5"
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/serving-runtime --grace-period=15
```

jin: i'll take lead for the next 30m and continue watching. next steps for triage: collect heap snapshots, nvprof if we see more cuda resets, capture slab maps and allocator histograms. command for heap dump:

jin: ```
curl http://localhost:8080/admin/dump_heap | gzip > /tmp/heap-1758882345.gz
```

sara: filing a post-incident ticket for eng-runtime: suspected root cause = paged-attention allocator fragmentation + long-lived KV cache items under variable seq lengths. assign to @alex and @jin for deeper allocator tracing and compaction work.

customer-ops: sent notice to affected customers: "We detected memory pressure in a subset of serving nodes and are applying mitigations. You may experience reduced throughput for up to 30 minutes. We'll update."

alex: cluster status: 2 nodes still at high mem pressure, scheduling rolling restarts for them in next 15m. will avoid simultaneous restarts of more than one GPU per AZ.

jin: monitored graphs look better on most nodes; canary stable. i'll stay oncall and escalate if OOM trend reappears. handing off to night oncall @jin (self) — alex leaving, reachable for 15m.

sara: quick note: if we see cudaDriverReset + immediate re-accumulation, capture /var/log/nvidia-installer and kernel logs for timeline.

jin: ack. handoff complete. incident status: mitigations applied (kv_trim aggressive, temporary eviction watermark, model fallback, container restarts), customer notifications sent, oncall lead continuing watch. will open follow-up for allocator fixes + automated compaction job.
